latest.title: Weekend Agent Challenge: Daybreak
latest.description: I build fast and lose track of what I've shipped. This always-on AWS agent wakes on a schedule, scans all 49 of my public GitHub repos with Amazon Nova, and emails a short brief before I even sit down: what is live, what has gone quiet, what needs a README, plus three things to fix. Built on Lambda, EventBridge Scheduler, Bedrock, and SES. It runs on its own and reports back, read-only. It reports, I decide.

latest.description: I have always wanted to build a personal knowledge graph. Something that connects my Slack conversations, emails, local files, and project context into one searchable, intelligent layer. I tried Obsidian for a while, and it is great for note-taking. But it always felt disconnected from my actual workflow. And if you want cloud sync, you are paying extra for it.

latest.title: Weekend Agent Challenge: PULSE — Your Autonomous AI Chief of Staff
latest.description:
Every morning, before I check my phone, a brief is already waiting for me. It covers my meetings, flags urgent emails, surfaces GitHub PRs that need review, tells me the weather, and gives me a priority score for the day. I did not ask for it. I did not click anything. An autonomous agent running on AWS assembled it while I was asleep.
That agent is PULSE — a Personal Unified Life and Productivity Executive that runs entirely unattended, triggered by a schedule, powered by Amazon Bedrock.

trending.title: AWS Strands Agents vs LangChain: A Practical Guide to Choosing the Right Framework
trending.description:
I learned LangChain at work, then saw AWS Strands Agents' tool-calling loop and wondered: is this the same thing with a different name? 
This article is the real answer, not a spec-sheet comparison, covering who owns the control logic (you vs. the model), boilerplate and debugging, deployment via Bedrock AgentCore vs. self-managed stacks, and a decision checklist for each. Includes a companion repo with both frameworks built side by side, tested live against Bedrock, so you can run them yourself.
